q1_what_did_you_play: The whole hand, in an order chosen so the Sparks are spent where they actually buy something. The hand costs 2 energy in total (Slow Burn 1, Duck and Cover 1, both attacks 0 printed), so affordability was never the constraint — sequencing was. Slow Burn goes first: it spends the 3 Sparks for 5 Block, 10 Burst Energy, Burst +5, and another +5 for being Skill-tagged. If I had led with an attack instead, that attack would have eaten all 3 Sparks to make a card free that was already printed at 0 — the Spark bank would have evaporated for literally nothing. With the bank cashed out, Kaboom! (7) and Rapid Fire (4 four times, all landing on Nibbit as the only enemy) go in for 23 damage free of charge, taking Nibbit from 43 to 20. Duck and Cover spends the last energy for 5 more Block, putting me at 10 Block against a telegraphed 12 — I eat 2 and end at 40/62.
q2_other_line_considered: Yes, briefly, and both alternatives were about ordering rather than selection. First: leading with Kaboom! or Rapid Fire before Slow Burn. That is the natural instinct — hit first, defend after — and it is the trap on this board, because the attacks are printed at 0 and consuming 3 Sparks to discount them to 0 is pure waste, and it would also leave Slow Burn unable to pay its 'Spend 3 Sparks' cost. Second: skipping the attacks entirely to carry the Sparks into a later turn, holding Slow Burn plus Duck and Cover for 10 Block and banking the Spark for some future costed attack. I rejected that quickly — I cannot see a future hand, 23 free damage on a 43 HP enemy is more than half its bar, and Slow Burn spends the Sparks anyway, so there is no line that both keeps the bank and uses Slow Burn. Beyond ordering there was no real selection question: every card in the hand is affordable simultaneously, so there is nothing to cut.
q3_what_it_gave_up: The Sparks. Playing Slow Burn spends the whole bank of 3, so I go into next turn at 0 Sparks and the next Attack I draw pays its printed cost. If the deck hands me an expensive attack next turn, that discount is gone. I also gave up nothing on the damage or defence side, which is what makes this turn thin as a decision — the full hand fits inside the energy, so I am not trading damage against block the way a tighter hand would force. The only genuine cost is spending a resource now that I cannot see the future value of.
q4_different_intent: No. The hand costs 2 energy in total and I have 2 energy, so I play all of it regardless of what Nibbit telegraphs — there is no card I would cut and nothing else to spend the energy on. If Nibbit had shown a defensive or buffing intent instead of Attack 12, Duck and Cover's 5 Block would have been wasted, but wasted is not the same as costly: there is no alternative use for that energy in this hand, so I would still play it. A very large attack would not change it either — 10 Block is the maximum this hand can produce, and I am already producing it. The only thing that would move me is an intent that made damage irrelevant or block actively harmful, and nothing like that is on the board.
